newsitem.title: INDIA: INSTANT VIEW -Indian stocks to firm on oil impasse.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -Indian stocks to firm on oil impasse.

text.p: Bombay stocks are seen edging higher at start on Tuesday after the ruling United Front coalition government late on Monday deferred a decision on whether to raise petroleum product prices to cap a mounting oil subsdiy bill.
The government has scheduled another meeting for June 27.
Following are the comments from the market after the postponement.
KETAN JHAVERI, CHIEF DEALER AT KOTAK SECURITES, INDIAN

"The market should improve after this postponement. But, a lot still depends on how people will take this news. The hike in petrol prices is an inevitable fact. The government has to take hard decision."
He said the market movement will also depend on price movement in shares of tobacco conglomerate ITC which fell nearly 10 percent on Monday.
SANJAY VAID, CHIEF DEALER AT LLOYDS SECURITIES

"The market could open somewhat higher. The postponement should have an immediate postive impact, because the deferral of the hike means that a lot of thinking is being done and indications are that even if it comes about, it would not be substantial."
BHARAT VORA, INSTITUTIONAL SALES DEALER AT BROKERS ANUJ
"The market will improve tomorrow. With the decision still not being taken, speculators will get a chance to get into the market."
Speculators had taken profits in anticipation of a petroleum price hike, but they can now rebuild positions, Vora said.
